title: Proper identity-open compact-support comparison is the inverse named mate
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$; put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $S_T=
u_T^*$ for exact derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] and $U_T=R
u_{T,*}$, with actual unit $\eta_T:1	o U_TS_T$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Let $f:X	o Y$ be a proper morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-proper-morphism], and take the compactification $c=(\mathrm{id}_X,f)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $F_c=Rf^{c,\mathrm{et}}_!$ and $P_c=Rf^{c,\mathrm{pro}}_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and $F=Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}$, $Q=Rf_{\mathrm{pro},*}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $e:F_c\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ and $q:P_c\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ be the canonical identifications obtained by removing identity extension by zero, using its sheafification identification degreewise and the derived associators [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. For $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $C_{c,L}:P_cS_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}S_YF_cL$ be the canonical compact-support comparison at the identity etale-origin witness [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison, def-sf-compact-support-site-comparison-construction], and let $b_{f,L}:S_YFL\xrightarrow{\sim}QS_XL$ be the specified direct-image counit mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Then, naturally in $L$,
$$S_Y(e_L)\circ C_{c,L}\circ q_{S_XL}^{-1}=b_{f,L}^{-1}.$$
The exact open-extension comparison $S_X(\mathrm{id}_X)_!^{\mathrm{et}}	o(\mathrm{id}_X)_!^{\mathrm{pro}}S_X$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], under the same identity identifications, is the identity both on module sheaves and after termwise descent. Thus the displayed equality uses the named mate, fixed by the ordinary pullback/direct-image counits, and the specified compact-support comparison, rather than a choice of isomorphism between their endpoints.

proof.text: Use the identity clause of openImmersionLowerShriekComparison_coherence for the fixed finite coefficient ring. Identify the two canonical identity-extension isomorphisms: leftAdjointUniq against the identity adjunction transported along upperStarId agrees with leftAdjointIdIso. The private adjoint_identity_iso proves this by expanding conjugation and the transported adjunction. This yields the specified equality on module sheaves, including empty schemes and zero sheaves.

proof.text: Package the sheaf equation as an equality of natural isomorphisms o followed by S(p) equals e followed by S. The private derive_identity_square applies exact derivation: preservation of vertical composition, naturality of the derived compositor in both variables, and its two identity laws give the equation in the unbounded derived category. Apply the fully faithful bounded-below inclusion; its compatibility with derived natural isomorphisms, compositors and identity comparisons gives the same equation in D+. This is precisely the properOpenSiteExtensionIso and the two identityOpen derived isomorphisms of the statement.

proof.text: Expand compactSupportSiteComparisonPlus at Compactification.ofIsProper f. Its inverse is Q(o inverse) followed by the inverse of the named direct-image mate at the identity extension. Expand the definitions of e and q and cancel the functor unitors. Naturality of the inverse named mate at e moves comparison pullback of the direct image of e across it. The remaining Q image is p inverse followed by o inverse followed by S(e), equal to the identity by step 2 and the two inverse laws. Functoriality cancels this identity, leaving exactly the inverse named mate. Extensionality gives equality of natural transformations.
